declared.title: The Relationship Between Eyewitness Confidence and Identification Accuracy: A New Synthesis
declared.venue: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
declared.foundIn: the coordinator's brief (« Wixted & Wells 2017 (Psychological Science in the Public Interest) »); OpenAlex search of its title (2026-11-23)

population: adult eyewitnesses in mock-crime lab studies and police field studies (the abstract speaks of the U.S. legal system)

findings.text: When memory is tested first and without contamination (fair lineup, blind administrator, confidence noted at once), confidence and accuracy are strongly related and high-confidence identifications are remarkably accurate

support.sentence: Under those conditions, mock-crime studies and police department field studies have consistently shown that, for adults, (a) confidence and accuracy are strongly related and (b) high-confidence suspect identifications are remarkably accurate.

findings.text: When testing conditions are not pristine (an unfair lineup, for example), even a high-confidence identification is seriously compromised

support.sentence: However, when certain non-pristine testing conditions prevail (e.g., when unfair lineups are used), the accuracy of even a high-confidence suspect ID is seriously compromised.

limits: a synthesis by two leading researchers, without a systematic search: classed as a narrative review
about recognizing a face in a lineup, not about remembering who said what in a meeting
contested: Berkowitz et al. 2020 and Fitzgerald et al. 2025 show conditions where high initial confidence is wrong in real cases
